title: PRD Addendum v4 — Screen Restructure to Portfolio, Candidates-Only Watchlist, Display Labels, Add-Position Location and Multiple Themes (D38-D40)

sections.heading: Change Record
sections.body: markdown: addendum v4.0 extends addendum v3 (which extends addendum v2, which extends addendum v1, which extends PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_v2) after owner decisions D38 (screen restructure), D39 (labels + Add-Position location, approved on ui_frontend_design_v4.html) and D40 (multiple themes System/Light/Dark), all CONFIRMED in brainstorm v2.3.0 of 2026-10-31. Scope of this addendum is exactly those three owner decisions. What it supersedes from addendum v3: (a) sidebar nav — Month Grid renamed to Portfolio; (b) the 'Two-View Watchlist' section — My Holdings moves OUT of Watchlist into Portfolio tabs, Watchlist becomes candidates-only; (c) 'Move to Holdings' action renamed 'Move to Portfolio'. No legacy FR is altered or deleted — v4 only adds FR-50 onward; every earlier requirement stays owned by its original document, and the FR ranges of PRD_DK_Bond_Tracker_v2, addendum v1, addendum v2 and addendum v3 remain unchanged.

sections.heading: Design Source
sections.body: UI truth: .IDE_Plans/design_drafts/ui_frontend_design_v4.html (approved by the owner on 2026-10-31) — it fixes the six-item sidebar (Dashboard, Portfolio, Watchlist, Financial Goals, Alerts, Settings), the Portfolio screen with My Holdings and Payouts tabs, the nine-column position registry, the Add Position form (start date, end date, auto-calculated tenure, credit day), the Payouts month grid, the candidates-only Watchlist with the Move to Portfolio action, and the four-chip status legend. Theme truth (D40): .IDE_Plans/design_drafts/ui_frontend_design_v5.html — the theme extension authored in parallel; this document references its path only and does not restate its palette. Structural wireframe: .IDE_Plans/design_drafts/dk_bond_tracker_ui_wireframe_design_v4.excalidraw.json.

sections.heading: Sidebar Navigation (D38)
sections.body: The sidebar navigation reads exactly Dashboard | Portfolio | Watchlist | Financial Goals | Alerts | Settings — six destinations in this order, with no other navigation item. Portfolio replaces the former Month Grid destination (D38). Dashboard keeps the money summary, Portfolio hosts owned positions behind its My Holdings and Payouts tabs, Watchlist holds research candidates, Financial Goals and Alerts remain destinations, and Settings stays a real, reachable screen.

sections.heading: Portfolio Screen (D38)
sections.body: Portfolio is the home of owned positions. It carries two tabs: 'My Holdings' — the position registry with the full field set, the row-click detail drawer carried over from the watchlist redesign, the Received and Next Payout columns and the payment-health statuses — and 'Payouts' — the month-grid pattern (companies x months, mark paid/unpaid, colored cells, auto-sort Danger top, On-going next, Matured bottom). The Add Position action lives inside Portfolio > My Holdings (D39). The status legend card renders on Portfolio showing Watching, On-going, Danger and Matured.

sections.heading: Watchlist Candidates Only (D38)
sections.body: The Watchlist is candidates only: a research list of companies not yet bought, each row carrying the purchase state Watching and the Move to Portfolio action. Allowed columns: Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Est. Yield, Source note, Action. There are no Invested, Received or Next Payout columns and no payment-health columns or status chips anywhere on the Watchlist (D38). Payment-health statuses — On-going, Danger, Matured — exist only on Portfolio surfaces and are derived from the Payouts grid: everything needs to reflect from the monthly grid.

sections.heading: Add Position and Move to Portfolio (D39)
sections.body: Approved on ui_frontend_design_v4.html (D39): the Add Position button sits inside Portfolio > My Holdings. Its form captures start date, end date, an auto-calculated tenure in months (read-only) and a credit day from 1 to 31, and the credit day drives the day-wise danger evaluation. Watchlist candidates convert through the Move to Portfolio action. Both paths funnel through the same D15 duplicate/active-position lock check before anything is written: a company whose position is already On-going or Danger cannot be added again, and after Matured a new purchase is allowed, which restarts the lifecycle at On-going or Danger.

sections.heading: Display Labels and Status Model (D39)
sections.body: Display relabels, engine values unchanged: Returned renders as Received, Completed renders as Matured, and neither 'Returned' nor 'Completed' is rendered as a label anywhere in the UI (D39). Two independent status dimensions: purchase state with the values Watching and Held (Held = owned position), and payment health with the values On-going, Danger and Matured derived from the Payouts grid (D38). The status legend on Portfolio shows all four rendered values, and Danger rows sort to the top of the Payouts grid with On-going next and Matured last.

sections.heading: Multiple Themes (D40)
sections.body: Three themes ship: System (follows the OS), Light (default) and Dark — selectable from a switcher in the header and from Settings > Appearance. The choice persists across restarts and is applied before first paint, so there is no flash of the wrong theme. All colors come from CSS custom properties — light tokens on :root, dark tokens on html[data-theme=dark] — System mode follows prefers-color-scheme live, an explicit Light or Dark choice overrides the OS, and the dark palette uses no pure black or pure white surfaces, WCAG AA contrast and desaturated accents. One theme decision renders every screen identically (D40).

sections.heading: Default Data
sections.body: A new installation starts empty: zero positions, zero candidates, zero payments — nothing is seeded (D37, reconfirmed by the D38 restructure under which Portfolio and Watchlist both start empty). The sample rows shown in the approved design are illustrative only and are never written to the database.

sections.heading: Out of Scope
sections.body: No live market data, no live rating or price feeds, no broker integrations — ratings, coupons and expected yields stay manual offline entries labeled as such wherever shown (D33). Beyond the three shipped theme modes there is no accent gallery and no custom theme editor (D40 option A only; option C not chosen). No cloud, no accounts, no server: email is the only outbound network use and only when the user configures their own SMTP. No legacy-format import — the product starts empty (D37). Android packaging and mobile apps remain out (D27). The acceptance holds: Phase-4 P&L acceptance only (L2 pending owner confirmation).

prd_items.statement: The product SHALL restructure its main surfaces so that owned positions are reachable only under the Portfolio screen (My Holdings and Payouts), the Watchlist holds candidates only, and payment-health statuses are rendered only on Portfolio surfaces (D38).

The sidebar navigation SHALL list exactly these destinations in this order — Dashboard, Portfolio, Watchlist, Financial Goals, Alerts, Settings — with Portfolio replacing the former Month Grid label and no additional navigation item (D38).
The Portfolio screen SHALL provide exactly two tabs, 'My Holdings' and 'Payouts', with My Holdings active by default, and switching between them SHALL keep the user on the Portfolio screen (D38).

The My Holdings tab SHALL render a position registry with the columns Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Yield, Frequency, Invested, Received, Next Payout and Status in that order, and selecting a row SHALL open the per-position detail drawer carried over from the watchlist redesign (D33) (D38).

The Add Position action SHALL live inside Portfolio > My Holdings; its form SHALL capture a start date, an end date, an auto-calculated tenure in whole months shown read-only, and a credit day from 1 to 31; and both the Add Position submit and the Watchlist Move to Portfolio action SHALL pass through the same D15 duplicate/active-position lock check before any row is written (D39).

The Payouts tab SHALL render the month-grid pattern — one row per company and one column per month — showing only the current month and past months and never future months; each cell SHALL show either the payment amount or the payment status; and rows SHALL auto-sort with Danger on top, On-going next and Matured at the bottom (D38).

The Watchlist SHALL be candidates-only with the columns Company/ISIN, Rating, Coupon, Est. Yield, Source note and Action, every candidate SHALL show the status Watching, and no Invested, Received, Next Payout or payment-health column SHALL appear anywhere in the Watchlist (D38).

The Move to Portfolio action SHALL convert a candidate into a position under the D15 lock: a company whose position is already On-going or Danger SHALL NOT be added again, and after Matured a new purchase SHALL be allowed and SHALL restart the lifecycle as On-going or Danger (D39).

The UI SHALL render the received-amount label as 'Received' and the finished-position label as 'Matured' while leaving the engine values Returned and Completed unchanged, so neither 'Returned' nor 'Completed' is rendered as a label anywhere (D39).

The product SHALL model purchase state as Watching or Held and payment health as On-going, Danger or Matured, SHALL derive payment health from the Payouts grid, SHALL render a status legend on the Portfolio screen, and SHALL sort Danger rows to the top of the Payouts grid with On-going next and Matured last (D38, D39).

The application SHALL ship three themes — System (follows the operating system), Light (default) and Dark — switchable from a header switcher and from Settings > Appearance, SHALL persist the choice across restarts in the browser localStorage key dk-theme, and SHALL apply the stored theme before first paint with no flash of the wrong theme (D40).

A new installation SHALL start with zero positions, zero candidates and zero payments — nothing is seeded — and the sample rows shown in the approved design SHALL be treated as illustrative only and never written to the database (D37; reconfirmed by the D38 restructure, under which Portfolio and Watchlist start empty) (D38).
